# STAR Interview Answers

Career stories in Situation / Task / Action / Result form. An agent reads this when
generating interview prep, and draws on it for cover letter narratives.

Write these once, properly. Most behavioral questions are a remix of five or six
real stories, so depth here pays back across every interview.

---

## <Question or theme, e.g. "Tell me about a time you had no playbook">

**Situation:** <Context. What was happening, who was involved, what was at stake.>

**Task:** <What you specifically were responsible for. Not the team, you.>

**Action:** <What you did, step by step. The most important section. Include the
false starts and what you changed after them; interviewers probe for exactly that.>

**Result:** <The outcome with a number. What changed because of the work, and what
you would do differently.>

**Good for:** <Which question types this answers: ambiguity, conflict, failure,
influence without authority, technical depth, leadership.>
